title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.

"""Load the released Grammar benchmark and reproduce the authors' train/test split.

Data source: repo/data/grammar.npy (shipped in the authors' TokenCore repository,
converted from the Label Studio export data/grammar_correction_labeled.json by
repo/tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py).

Split: the authors' eval.py was not released, but a compiled bytecode copy of it
(eval.cpython-310.pyc, source path d:\\Github\\TokenCore\\eval.py) was found next to
the demo notebook.  Disassembling it recovers `split_anomaly_data` verbatim:

    def split_anomaly_data(X, y, z, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42):
        y = np.array(y)
        n_train = int(len(X) * train_ratio)
        normal_indices = np.where(y == 0)[0]
        np.random.seed(random_state)
        train_indices = np.random.choice(normal_indices, size=n_train, replace=False)
        test_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(X)), train_indices)
        X_train = [X[i] for i in train_indices]
        y_train = y[train_indices]
        X_test = [X[i] for i in test_indices]
        y_test = y[test_indices]
        z_train = [z[i] for i in train_indices]
        z_test = [z[i] for i in test_indices]
        return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test

This module re-implements exactly that semantics (paper R6: 50% normal documents as
training data, the rest of the data - both normal and anomalous - as test set).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

REPO_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "repo"
GRAMMAR_NPY = REPO_DIR / "data" / "grammar.npy"


def load_grammar(path: str | Path = GRAMMAR_NPY) -> dict:
    """Load the released Grammar benchmark into a canonical dict.

    Returns dict with keys: sentences, tokens (list of list of gold word tokens),
    token_labels (list of list of 0/1), doc_labels (list of 0/1).
    """
    path = Path(path)
    data = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    sentences = list(data["sentences"])
    tokens = list(data["tokens"])
    labels = list(data["labels"])

    assert len(sentences) == len(tokens) == len(labels), "ragged benchmark file"

    # R10: Grammar = 300 documents, 30 anomalous (10% anomaly rate).
    assert len(tokens) == 300, f"expected 300 documents, found {len(tokens)}"

    doc_labels = []
    for i, labs in enumerate(labels):
        labs = [int(x) for x in labs]
        assert set(labs) <= {0, 1}, f"doc {i}: unexpected label values {set(labs)}"
        assert len(labs) == len(tokens[i]), f"doc {i}: token/label length mismatch"
        # R11: a document is anomalous iff it contains at least one anomalous token.
        doc_labels.append(1 if any(labs) else 0)

    n_anom = sum(doc_labels)
    assert n_anom == 30, f"expected 30 anomalous documents, found {n_anom}"
    n_norm = len(doc_labels) - n_anom
    assert n_norm == 270, f"expected 270 normal documents, found {n_norm}"

    return {
        "name": "grammar",
        "sentences": sentences,
        "tokens": tokens,
        "token_labels": labels,
        "doc_labels": doc_labels,
    }


def split_anomaly_data(X, y, z, train_ratio: float = 0.5, random_state: int = 42):
    """Verbatim re-implementation of the authors' eval.split_anomaly_data.

    X: list of documents (each a list of word tokens)
    y: document-level labels (0 normal / 1 anomalous)
    z: token-level labels (list of list of 0/1)

    Training documents are drawn only from the normal ones (R3: the memory bank
    never sees anomalous tokens); every document that is not picked for training
    goes to the test set, normal and anomalous alike (R6).
    """
    y = np.array(y)
    n_train = int(len(X) * train_ratio)
    normal_indices = np.where(y == 0)[0]
    np.random.seed(random_state)
    train_indices = np.random.choice(normal_indices, size=n_train, replace=False)
    test_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(X)), train_indices)
    X_train = [X[i] for i in train_indices]
    y_train = y[train_indices]
    X_test = [X[i] for i in test_indices]
    y_test = y[test_indices]
    z_train = [z[i] for i in train_indices]
    z_test = [z[i] for i in test_indices]
    return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test


def split_doc_indices(doc_labels, train_ratio: float = 0.5, random_state: int = 42):
    """Same split as split_anomaly_data, but returning document index arrays."""
    y = np.asarray(doc_labels)
    n_train = int(len(y) * train_ratio)
    normal_indices = np.where(y == 0)[0]
    np.random.seed(random_state)
    train_indices = np.random.choice(normal_indices, size=n_train, replace=False)
    test_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(y)), train_indices)
    return np.sort(train_indices), np.sort(test_indices)


def summarize_split(data: dict, train_idx, test_idx) -> dict:
    """Counts/rates of a split, used for the intermediate checks."""
    tok_train = [len(data["tokens"][i]) for i in train_idx]
    tok_test = [len(data["tokens"][i]) for i in test_idx]
    pos_test = int(sum(sum(int(x) for x in data["token_labels"][i]) for i in test_idx))
    pos_train = int(sum(sum(int(x) for x in data["token_labels"][i]) for i in train_idx))
    return {
        "n_train_docs": int(len(train_idx)),
        "n_test_docs": int(len(test_idx)),
        "n_test_normal": int(sum(1 for i in test_idx if data["doc_labels"][i] == 0)),
        "n_test_anomalous": int(sum(1 for i in test_idx if data["doc_labels"][i] == 1)),
        "n_train_tokens": int(sum(tok_train)),
        "n_test_tokens": int(sum(tok_test)),
        "n_train_positive_tokens": pos_train,
        "n_test_positive_tokens": pos_test,
        "test_token_positive_rate": pos_test / max(1, sum(tok_test)),
        "test_doc_positive_rate": float(np.mean([data["doc_labels"][i] for i in test_idx])),
    }

"""BERT-base front-end: contextual word embeddings by element-wise max pooling over subwords.

This is a batched re-implementation of the released repo/align.py
`extract_word_embeddings` (the authors' active code path): tokenize each document
with `is_split_into_words=True`, run the model, drop the [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD]
positions, and aggregate the subword vectors of every gold word unit with an
element-wise max (paper Eq. 1, requirements R2/R9).  Only the batching differs
from the authors' per-sentence loop; `reproduce.py` cross-checks the two on
several documents and asserts numerical equality.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import torch


@torch.no_grad()
def extract_word_embeddings_batched(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    all_tokens,
    all_labels=None,
    batch_size: int = 32,
    device: str = "cpu",
    log=print,
):
    """Return a list (one entry per document) of lists of dicts.

    Each dict has keys: token, embedding (768,), label, subword_position,
    n_subwords - the same structure as the authors' align.py output.
    """
    if all_labels is None:
        all_labels = [None] * len(all_tokens)
    model = model.to(device).eval()

    n_words_total = 0
    n_dropped_words = 0
    result_sentences = []

    for start in range(0, len(all_tokens), batch_size):
        batch_tokens = list(all_tokens[start : start + batch_size])
        batch_labels = list(all_labels[start : start + batch_size])
        encoded = tokenizer(
            batch_tokens,
            is_split_into_words=True,
            return_tensors="pt",
            truncation=True,
            padding=True,
        )
        input_ids = encoded["input_ids"].to(device)
        attention_mask = encoded["attention_mask"].to(device)
        outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)
        last_hidden_state = outputs.last_hidden_state

        for b in range(len(batch_tokens)):
            tokens = batch_tokens[b]
            labels = batch_labels[b]
            word_ids = encoded.word_ids(batch_index=b)
            hidden = last_hidden_state[b]

            # group subword positions by gold word index (order-preserving)
            groups: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
            for token_position, word_idx in enumerate(word_ids):
                if word_idx is None:
                    continue  # skip [CLS], [SEP], [PAD]
                groups.setdefault(word_idx, []).append(token_position)

            sentence_data = []
            for word_idx in range(len(tokens)):
                if word_idx not in groups:
                    # align.py would silently drop such a word; flag it loudly
                    n_dropped_words += 1
                    log(f"  [WARN] word {word_idx} '{tokens[word_idx]}' produced no subword")
                    continue
                positions = groups[word_idx]
                subword_vecs = hidden[positions].cpu().numpy()
                emb = np.max(np.stack(subword_vecs), axis=0)  # Eq. (1): element-wise max
                sentence_data.append(
                    {
                        "token": tokens[word_idx],
                        "embedding": emb,
                        "label": (int(labels[word_idx]) if labels is not None else None),
                        "subword_position": positions,
                        "n_subwords": len(positions),
                    }
                )
                n_words_total += 1
            result_sentences.append(sentence_data)

    log(
        f"extracted {n_words_total} word embeddings from {len(all_tokens)} documents "
        f"(dropped words: {n_dropped_words})"
    )
    return result_sentences


def flatten_docs(sentence_data):
    """Pool per-document word dicts into one (n_tokens, 768) matrix + labels + lengths.

    Same flatten as the demo notebook:
        X = np.array([item['embedding'] for sent in data for item in sent])
        z = [item['label'] for sent in data for item in sent]
    """
    X = np.array([item["embedding"] for sent in sentence_data for item in sent])
    z = [int(item["label"]) for sent in sentence_data for item in sent]
    lengths = [len(sent) for sent in sentence_data]
    return X, z, lengths


def load_backbone(model_name_or_dir: str, device: str = "cpu"):
    """Load BERT-base-uncased tokenizer+model from a local dir or the HF hub."""
    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name_or_dir)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name_or_dir)
    model.eval()
    return tokenizer, model.to(device)

"""Adapter over the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py detector.

The file is loaded by path (it is not an importable package) and used exactly as
in the demo notebook / the authors' benchmark code:

    model = TokenCore()            # n_neighbors=1 -> score = distance to the
    model.fit(X_train)             #                  nearest memory-bank entry
    score = model.decision_function(X_test)

The benchmark bytecode (run_anomaly_detection_benchmark) instantiates TextCore
with {'n_neighbors': [1]}, so n_neighbors=1 is the paper's configuration.
NearestNeighbors' default metric is Euclidean (minkowski p=2) - paper Eq. (2).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "repo"


def load_authors_tokencore():
    """Import the authors' TokenCore class without touching their file."""
    path = REPO_DIR / "TokenCore.py"
    name = "authors_tokencore"
    if name in sys.modules:
        return sys.modules[name].TokenCore
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.TokenCore


def make_detector():
    """Authors' detector, paper configuration (n_neighbors=1)."""
    TokenCore = load_authors_tokencore()
    return TokenCore(n_neighbors=1)


def fit_and_score(X_train, X_test):
    """Fit the memory bank on the normal-training token embeddings (R3) and
    return one nearest-neighbour distance per test token (R4)."""
    import numpy as np

    assert len(X_train) > 0, "empty memory bank"
    assert X_train.shape[1] == X_test.shape[1], "embedding width mismatch"
    clf = make_detector()
    clf.fit(X_train)
    scores = np.asarray(clf.decision_function(X_test), dtype=np.float64)
    assert scores.shape[0] == X_test.shape[0]
    assert np.isfinite(scores).all(), "non-finite anomaly scores"
    return scores

"""Metric layer: pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC and aggregated document-level scores.

Token-level metrics follow the authors' recovered evaluate_model() exactly:

    token_roc_auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, scores)          # pooled over ALL test tokens
    precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_test, scores)
    token_pr_auc = auc(recall, precision)

Document-level scores aggregate each document's token scores (paper Eq. 3 uses the
mean; the authors' evaluate_model used np.max per sentence - both are reported).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import auc, precision_recall_curve, roc_auc_score


def token_level_metrics(y_true, scores) -> dict:
    """Pooled (micro) token-level AUROC / AUPRC over all test tokens."""
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=int)
    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
    assert y_true.shape == scores.shape
    assert set(np.unique(y_true)) == {0, 1}, "token-level AUROC needs both classes"
    roc = float(roc_auc_score(y_true, scores))
    precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_true, scores)
    pr = float(auc(recall, precision))
    return {"auroc": roc, "auprc": pr, "n": int(len(y_true)), "n_positive": int(y_true.sum())}


def document_scores(token_scores, doc_lengths, aggregation: str = "mean") -> np.ndarray:
    """Aggregate token scores into one score per document (paper Eq. 3: mean).

    aggregation: 'mean' (paper Eq. 3) or 'max' (the aggregation used inside the
    authors' recovered evaluate_model for sentence-level evaluation).
    """
    token_scores = np.asarray(token_scores, dtype=np.float64)
    doc_scores = []
    start = 0
    for length in doc_lengths:
        end = start + length
        chunk = token_scores[start:end]
        if aggregation == "mean":
            doc_scores.append(np.mean(chunk))
        elif aggregation == "max":
            doc_scores.append(np.max(chunk))
        else:
            raise ValueError(aggregation)
        start = end
    assert start == len(token_scores), "token scores / document lengths mismatch"
    return np.asarray(doc_scores)


def document_level_metrics(doc_labels, token_scores, doc_lengths, aggregation: str = "mean") -> dict:
    doc_scores = document_scores(token_scores, doc_lengths, aggregation)
    y = np.asarray(doc_labels, dtype=int)
    assert set(np.unique(y)) == {0, 1}, "document-level AUROC needs both classes"
    roc = float(roc_auc_score(y, doc_scores))
    precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(y, doc_scores)
    pr = float(auc(recall, precision))
    return {"auroc": roc, "auprc": pr, "aggregation": aggregation, "n": int(len(y)),
            "n_positive": int(y.sum())}


def random_control(n_tokens, positive_rate, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Sanity control: random scores must give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    n_pos = max(1, int(round(positive_rate * n_tokens)))
    n_neg = max(1, n_tokens - n_pos)
    y = np.array([1] * n_pos + [0] * n_neg)
    scores = rng.rand(len(y))
    roc = float(roc_auc_score(y, scores))
    precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(y, scores)
    pr = float(auc(recall, precision))
    return {"auroc": roc, "auprc": pr, "positive_rate": n_pos / len(y)}


def hand_rolled_auroc(y_true, scores) -> float:
    """Mann-Whitney U formulation of AUROC, for metric parity checking."""
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=int)
    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
    pos = scores[y_true == 1]
    neg = scores[y_true == 0]
    greater = (pos[:, None] > neg[None, :]).sum()
    equal = (pos[:, None] == neg[None, :]).sum()
    return float((greater + 0.5 * equal) / (len(pos) * len(neg)))


def check_metric_parity(seed: int = 0, n: int = 500, atol: float = 1e-12) -> dict:
    """Verify the metric plumbing on synthetic data (guards against swapped args)."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    y = rng.randint(0, 2, size=n)
    s = rng.rand(n)
    roc = float(roc_auc_score(y, s))
    parity = abs(roc - hand_rolled_auroc(y, s)) < atol
    assert parity, "hand-rolled AUROC disagrees with sklearn"
    # deterministic closed-form case: scores already ranked with 4 positives first
    y2 = np.array([1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0])
    s2 = np.array([0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2])
    assert abs(roc_auc_score(y2, s2) - 1.0) < 1e-12
    assert abs(hand_rolled_auroc(y2, s2) - 1.0) < 1e-12
    assert abs(roc_auc_score(y2, s2[::-1]) - 0.0) < 1e-12
    return {"auroc_random_synthetic": roc, "parity_ok": True}

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduce the TokenCore Grammar result (claim C1: token-level AUROC on Grammar).

Pipeline (paper "Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection", Sec. 5-6):
  1. load the released Grammar benchmark (repo/data/grammar.npy; 300 docs, 30 anomalous),
  2. split with the authors' own split function (recovered from their compiled
     eval.py: 50% of the documents, drawn from the normal ones only, seed 42)
     -> memory-bank training documents; the rest (normal + anomalous) is the test set,
  3. embed every document with BERT-base-uncased, max-pooling subword vectors into
     word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1),
  4. build the memory bank from the normal-training token embeddings only and score
     every test token by its nearest-neighbour Euclidean distance (Eq. 2) with the
     authors' unmodified TokenCore class,
  5. pool all test tokens for token-level AUROC/AUPRC; mean-aggregate token scores
     per document for document-level AUROC/AUPRC (Eq. 3),
  6. write results/metrics.json.

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                 # full run, backbone bert-base-uncased, seed 42
  python reproduce.py --smoke         # 10-document end-to-end smoke test
  python reproduce.py --no-extra-seeds
  python reproduce.py --backbones bert-base-uncased bert-base-cased   # sensitivity
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import contextlib
import io
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_anomaly_data, split_doc_indices, summarize_split
from detector import fit_and_score
from embed_bert import extract_word_embeddings_batched, flatten_docs, load_backbone
from evaluate import (
    check_metric_parity,
    document_level_metrics,
    random_control,
    token_level_metrics,
)

DEFAULT_SEED = 42          # authors' eval.py default (recovered from bytecode)
EXTRA_SEEDS = [0, 1, 2]    # split-seed sensitivity spread
PAPER_TARGET_C1 = 0.6371   # Table 1, Token section, TokenCore, Grammar ROC
TOLERANCE = 0.02           # absolute band from the claim contract


def log(msg=""):
    print(msg, flush=True)


def resolve_backbone_dir(name: str) -> str:
    cache = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    if cache:
        candidate = Path(cache) / "models" / name
        if (candidate / "config.json").exists():
            return str(candidate)
    return name  # fall back to the HuggingFace hub


def embed_dataset(model, tokenizer, data, batch_size, device, log=log):
    t0 = time.time()
    sentence_data = extract_word_embeddings_batched(
        model, tokenizer, data["tokens"], all_labels=data["token_labels"],
        batch_size=batch_size, device=device, log=log,
    )
    dt = time.time() - t0
    # alignment coverage: every gold word unit must receive exactly one embedding (R9)
    n_gold = sum(len(t) for t in data["tokens"])
    n_emb = sum(len(s) for s in sentence_data)
    assert n_emb == n_gold, f"alignment coverage {n_emb}/{n_gold}"
    # labels must survive the alignment unchanged
    flat_labels = [item["label"] for sent in sentence_data for item in sent]
    gold_labels = [int(x) for labs in data["token_labels"] for x in labs]
    assert flat_labels == gold_labels, "token labels misaligned with gold annotations"
    log(f"[check] alignment coverage {n_emb}/{n_gold} = 1.0 in {dt:.1f}s")
    return sentence_data, dt


def crosscheck_align_repo(model, tokenizer, data, n_docs: int, device: str):
    """Assert the batched extractor equals the authors' released align.py on n_docs."""
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "repo"))
    import align as authors_align

    buf = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
        ref = authors_align.extract_word_embeddings(
            model=model,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            all_tokens=data["tokens"][:n_docs],
            all_labels=data["token_labels"][:n_docs],
            model_name="local",
            local_cache_dir="unused",
            device=device,
        )
    mine = extract_word_embeddings_batched(
        model, tokenizer, data["tokens"][:n_docs], all_labels=data["token_labels"][:n_docs],
        batch_size=4, device=device, log=lambda *_: None,
    )
    ref_X, ref_z, ref_len = flatten_docs(ref)
    my_X, my_z, my_len = flatten_docs(mine)
    assert ref_z == my_z and ref_len == my_len, "align.py cross-check: labels/lengths differ"
    diff = float(np.max(np.abs(ref_X - my_X)))
    assert diff < 1e-3, f"align.py cross-check failed: max |diff| = {diff}"
    return diff


def crosscheck_cached_npz(sentence_data):
    """Optional consistency probe against a previously cached embedding file."""
    cache = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    path = Path(cache) / "grammar_emb" / "bert-base-uncased.npz" if cache else None
    if not path or not path.exists():
        return None
    cached = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)["data"]
    diffs = [float(np.max(np.abs(np.asarray(cached[i]["emb"]) -
                                 np.stack([it["embedding"] for it in sentence_data[i]]))))
             for i in range(len(sentence_data))]
    return {"max_abs_diff": max(diffs), "mean_abs_diff": float(np.mean(diffs))}

    train_docs = [sentence_data[i] for i in train_idx]
    test_docs = [sentence_data[i] for i in test_idx]

"""Diagnostic: split-seed sweep for both BERT backbones on the Grammar benchmark.

Embeds all 300 documents once per backbone (authors' max-pooling extractor),
then repeats the authors' split (50% normal-only training docs) over many seeds
and reports the distribution of token-level AUROC/AUPRC.
"""
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_doc_indices
from detector import fit_and_score
from embed_bert import extract_word_embeddings_batched, flatten_docs, load_backbone
from evaluate import token_level_metrics, document_level_metrics


def resolve(name):
    cache = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    d = Path(cache) / "models" / name
    return str(d) if (d / "config.json").exists() else name


def main():
    torch.set_num_threads(min(8, os.cpu_count() or 1))
    data = load_grammar()
    n_seeds = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 30
    seeds = list(range(n_seeds))

    for backbone in ["bert-base-uncased", "bert-base-cased"]:
        tok, model = load_backbone(resolve(backbone), device="cpu")
        t0 = time.time()
        sd = extract_word_embeddings_batched(model, tok, data["tokens"],
                                             all_labels=data["token_labels"],
                                             batch_size=32, device="cpu",
                                             log=lambda *_: None)
        print(f"{backbone}: embedded in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s")
        rows = []
        for seed in seeds:
            tr, te = split_doc_indices(data["doc_labels"], random_state=seed)
            Xtr, ztr, _ = flatten_docs([sd[i] for i in tr])
            Xte, zte, lens = flatten_docs([sd[i] for i in te])
            s = fit_and_score(Xtr, Xte)
            m = token_level_metrics(zte, s)
            dmean = document_level_metrics([data["doc_labels"][i] for i in te], s, lens, "mean")
            dmax = document_level_metrics([data["doc_labels"][i] for i in te], s, lens, "max")
            rows.append((seed, m["auroc"], m["auprc"], dmean["auroc"], dmax["auroc"]))
        arr = np.array([(r[1], r[2], r[3], r[4]) for r in rows])
        print(f"  token AUROC: mean {arr[:,0].mean():.4f} std {arr[:,0].std():.4f} "
              f"min {arr[:,0].min():.4f} max {arr[:,0].max():.4f}")
        print(f"  token AUPRC: mean {arr[:,1].mean():.4f} std {arr[:,1].std():.4f} "
              f"min {arr[:,1].min():.4f} max {arr[:,1].max():.4f}")
        print(f"  doc AUROC (mean agg): mean {arr[:,2].mean():.4f} std {arr[:,2].std():.4f}")
        print(f"  doc AUROC (max agg):  mean {arr[:,3].mean():.4f} std {arr[:,3].std():.4f}")
        s42 = [r for r in rows if r[0] == 42][0]
        print(f"  seed 42: token AUROC {s42[1]:.4f} AUPRC {s42[2]:.4f} | "
              f"doc mean {s42[3]:.4f} doc max {s42[4]:.4f}")
        for target in [0.6371]:
            hits = [r[0] for r in rows if abs(r[1] - target) <= 0.02]
            print(f"  seeds within +/-0.02 of {target}: {hits}")
        del model
        torch.cuda.empty_cache if hasattr(torch.cuda, "empty_cache") else None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

args.content:
"""Decisive isolation test.

Feed the word-level 768-d embeddings that ship with this workspace's data cache
(grammar_emb/bert-base-uncased.npz - the same word-level alignment the authors'
align.py produces; repo/data/grammar.npy itself carries only text/labels, no
embeddings) through the UNCHANGED detector (authors' TokenCore) and the
recovered split_anomaly_data, and print token-level AUROC/AUPRC.

Interpretation:
  * if this lands near the paper value, the gap is in my embedding extraction;
  * if it lands near my re-extracted value, extraction is exonerated and the gap
    lives in the split/scorer.

Also compares, per word: cosine(re-extracted, cached) and which hidden-layer
choice (last / -2 / mean of last 4) matches the cache best.
"""
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_doc_indices, summarize_split
from detector import fit_and_score
from embed_bert import extract_word_embeddings_batched, flatten_docs, load_backbone
from evaluate import token_level_metrics, document_level_metrics, random_control

TARGET = 0.6371


def cached_doc_matrices():
    cache = os.environ["REPRO_DATA_CACHE"]
    z = np.load(Path(cache) / "grammar_emb" / "bert-base-uncased.npz", allow_pickle=True)["data"]
    order = [int(d["doc_id"]) for d in z]
    assert order == list(range(300)), "cache doc order"
    embs = [np.asarray(d["emb"], dtype=np.float64) for d in z]
    labels = [[int(x) for x in d["labels"]] for d in z]
    doc_labels = [int(d["doc_label"]) for d in z]
    return embs, labels, doc_labels


def run_cached(tag):
    embs, labels, doc_labels = cached_doc_matrices()
    tr, te = split_doc_indices(doc_labels, random_state=42)
    Xtr = np.concatenate([embs[i] for i in tr]); ztr = [x for i in tr for x in labels[i]]
    Xte = np.concatenate([embs[i] for i in te]); zte = [x for i in te for x in labels[i]]
    lens = [len(embs[i]) for i in te]
    assert sum(ztr) == 0, "anomalous tokens in bank"
    s = fit_and_score(Xtr, Xte)
    m = token_level_metrics(zte, s)
    dm = document_level_metrics([doc_labels[i] for i in te], s, lens, "mean")
    dx = document_level_metrics([doc_labels[i] for i in te], s, lens, "max")
    print(f"[{tag}] CACHED embeddings + authors' split(42) + authors' TokenCore:")
    print(f"   token AUROC {m['auroc']:.4f}  token AUPRC {m['auprc']:.4f}  "
          f"(bank {Xtr.shape[0]} tokens, test {Xte.shape[0]} tokens, {m['n_positive']} anomalous)")
    print(f"   doc AUROC mean-agg {dm['auroc']:.4f} | max-agg {dx['auroc']:.4f}")
    print(f"   distance to paper target {TARGET}: {abs(m['auroc']-TARGET):.4f}")
    return m, dm, dx


def main():
    # ---- isolation test on cached embeddings ----
    m_cached, dm_cached, dx_cached = run_cached("isolation")

    # ---- my re-extracted embeddings through the identical path ----
    torch.set_num_threads(min(8, os.cpu_count() or 1))
    data = load_grammar()
    tok, model = load_backbone(str(Path(os.environ["REPRO_DATA_CACHE"]) / "models" / "bert-base-uncased"),
                               device="cpu")
    sd = extract_word_embeddings_batched(model, tok, data["tokens"], all_labels=data["token_labels"],
                                         batch_size=32, device="cpu", log=lambda *_: None)
    tr, te = split_doc_indices(data["doc_labels"], random_state=42)
    Xtr, ztr, _ = flatten_docs([sd[i] for i in tr])
    Xte, zte, lens = flatten_docs([sd[i] for i in te])
    s = fit_and_score(Xtr, Xte)
    m_mine = token_level_metrics(zte, s)
    print(f"[re-extracted] token AUROC {m_mine['auroc']:.4f}  token AUPRC {m_mine['auprc']:.4f}  "
          f"(same split/detector)")
    print(f"   |cached - re-extracted| AUROC: {abs(m_cached['auroc']-m_mine['auroc']):.6f}")

    # ---- per-word embedding comparison: cosine + nearest-neighbour identity ----
    embs_cached, labels_cached, _ = cached_doc_matrices()
    X_all_mine, _, _ = flatten_docs(sd)
    X_all_cached = np.concatenate(embs_cached)
    assert X_all_mine.shape == X_all_cached.shape
    cos = np.sum(X_all_mine * X_all_cached, axis=1) / (
        np.linalg.norm(X_all_mine, axis=1) * np.linalg.norm(X_all_cached, axis=1))
    max_abs = np.max(np.abs(X_all_mine - X_all_cached))
    print(f"[embedding comparison] n_words={len(cos)} mean_cos={cos.mean():.6f} "
          f"min_cos={cos.min():.6f} max_abs_diff={max_abs:.3e}")
    # nearest-neighbour identity check on 200 random test words

    idx = rng.choice(Xte.shape[0], size=min(200, Xte.shape[0]), replace=False)
    agree = 0

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduce the TokenCore Grammar result (claim C1: token-level AUROC on Grammar).

Pipeline (paper "Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection", Sec. 5-6):
  1. load the released Grammar benchmark (repo/data/grammar.npy; 300 docs, 30 anomalous),
  2. split with the authors' own split function (recovered from their compiled
     eval.py: 50% of the documents, drawn from the normal ones only, seed 42)
     -> memory-bank training documents; the rest (normal + anomalous) is the test set,
  3. embed every document with BERT, max-pooling subword vectors into word units
     aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1),
  4. build the memory bank from the normal-training token embeddings only and score
     every test token by its nearest-neighbour Euclidean distance (Eq. 2) with the
     authors' unmodified TokenCore class,
  5. pool all test tokens for token-level AUROC/AUPRC; mean-aggregate token scores
     per document for document-level AUROC/AUPRC (Eq. 3),
  6. write results/metrics.json.

code defaults to bert-base-cased (align.py model_name, demo notebook cell 1) and

def load_backbone(model_name_or_dir: str, device: str = "cpu"):
    """Load a BERT tokenizer+model from a local dir or the HF hub."""
    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name_or_dir)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name_or_dir)
    model.eval()
    return tokenizer, model.to(device)


def resolve_backbone(name: str) -> str:
    """Prefer a locally cached backbone (REPRO_DATA_CACHE/models/<name>) over the hub."""
    import os
    from pathlib import Path

    cache = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    if cache:
        d = Path(cache) / "models" / name
        if (d / "config.json").exists():
            return str(d)
    return name


def _encode_batch(tokenizer, all_tokens, batch_size: int = 32):
    """Tokenize pre-split word lists; returns the fast-tokenizer encoding object."""
    enc = tokenizer(list(all_tokens), is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt",
                    truncation=True, padding=True)
    return enc


def load_authors_align():
    """Import the authors' repo/align.py by path without touching their file."""
    import importlib.util
    import sys
    from pathlib import Path

    path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "repo" / "align.py"
    name = "authors_align"
    if name in sys.modules:
        return sys.modules[name]
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


@torch.no_grad()
def extract_word_embeddings_authors(model, tokenizer, all_tokens, all_labels=None, device="cpu"):

    for the batched extractor above.

    return align.extract_word_embeddings(
        model, tokenizer, all_tokens=list(all_tokens), all_labels=list(all_labels), device=device

"""Manager-requested control: StandardScaler (fit on the memory bank) before the
nearest-neighbour scorer, bert-base-uncased, split seed 42.

Decides whether feature standardisation - present in the authors' eval.py only as
an unused import - can reconcile the uncased run with the paper value.
"""
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_doc_indices
from detector import fit_and_score
from embed_bert import extract_word_embeddings_batched, flatten_docs, load_backbone, resolve_backbone
from evaluate import token_level_metrics, document_level_metrics

torch.set_num_threads(min(8, os.cpu_count() or 1))
data = load_grammar()
tok, model = load_backbone(resolve_backbone("bert-base-uncased"), device="cpu")
sd = extract_word_embeddings_batched(model, tok, data["tokens"], data["token_labels"],
                                     batch_size=32, device="cpu", log=lambda *a, **k: None)

tr, te = split_doc_indices(data["doc_labels"], random_state=42)
Xtr, ztr, _ = flatten_docs([sd[i] for i in tr])
Xte, zte, lens = flatten_docs([sd[i] for i in te])

sc = fit_and_score(Xtr, Xte)
m = token_level_metrics(zte, sc)
dm = document_level_metrics([data["doc_labels"][i] for i in te], sc, lens, "mean")
print(f"[raw/uncased/seed42]            token AUROC {m['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC {m['auprc']:.4f} | doc AUROC {dm['auroc']:.4f}")

scaler = StandardScaler().fit(Xtr)  # statistics from memory-bank tokens only
Xtr_s = scaler.transform(Xtr)
Xte_s = scaler.transform(Xte)
sc2 = fit_and_score(Xtr_s, Xte_s)
m2 = token_level_metrics(zte, sc2)
dm2 = document_level_metrics([data["doc_labels"][i] for i in te], sc2, lens, "mean")
print(f"[scaled/uncased/seed42]         token AUROC {m2['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC {m2['auprc']:.4f} | doc AUROC {dm2['auroc']:.4f}")

# also: scaler fit on ALL (bank+test) tokens, in case the authors scaled globally
scaler2 = StandardScaler().fit(np.concatenate([Xtr, Xte]))
sc3 = fit_and_score(scaler2.transform(Xtr), scaler2.transform(Xte))
m3 = token_level_metrics(zte, sc3)
print(f"[scaled_global/uncased/seed42]  token AUROC {m3['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC {m3['auprc']:.4f}")

target = 0.6371
for name, mm in [("raw", m), ("scaled_bank", m2), ("scaled_global", m3)]:
    print(f"  -> {name}: |diff to {target}| = {abs(mm['auroc'] - target):.4f} "
          f"({'INSIDE' if abs(mm['auroc'] - target) <= 0.02 else 'outside'} +/-0.02 band)")

target.statement: TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar dataset
target.table_ref: Table 1, Token section, row TokenCore, column Grammar ROC

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The TokenCore pipeline is faithfully implemented: BERT-base-uncased last hidden states, element-wise max pooling over subwords to word level (verified against the authors' align.py to 5e-6), a memory bank of all 1,327 normal-training word tokens (0 positive tokens), Euclidean 1-NN token scores, and mean (and max) document aggregation. The Grammar split follows the authors' recovered split_anomaly_data (int(300*0.5)=150 normal docs, seed 42), yielding 150 test docs (120 normal + 30 anomalous) and 47 anomalous test tokens. The measured token-level AUROC is 0.6137 at seed 42, 0.0234 below the 0.6371 target and outside the 0.02 tolerance; across four uncased seeds the mean is 0.5998 ± 0.0248. The implementer's own diagnostics (A13) show the authors' released code defaults to bert-base-cased and that configuration yields 0.6365 (diff 0.0047) at seed 42, so the miss is attributable primarily to the paper-vs-code backbone ambiguity (the run correctly follows the paper text per R1) rather than to a method substitution. No baselines (R8) were run and the SMS/Review claims were not attempted, so only the Grammar TokenCore pipeline is verified. No number is hard-coded or copied; the reported metric is computed live on the test tokens, and nothing in the target run is scaled down.

requirement_check.evidence: TokenCore uses bert-base-uncased last-hidden-state embeddings with element-wise max pooling over subwords (metrics_json config), and the extractor matches the authors' align.py to max|diff|=5.25e-06. However, the 'all methods including baselines share the same embeddings' clause is untested because no baselines were run in the clean re-run.

config.subword_to_word_pooling='element-wise max over subword vectors (paper Eq. 1)'; the authors' align2.py disassembly uses np.max(np.stack(current_subwords),axis=0) and the batched extractor reproduces it (max|diff|=5.25e-06).
memory_bank='all word-level token embeddings of the normal training documents'; seed-42 split has n_train_positive_tokens=0 and a 1,327-token bank drawn only from the 150 normal training docs.
distance_metric='Euclidean nearest neighbour (paper Eq. 2, sklearn minkowski p=2)', n_neighbors=1; token scores are min distances to the bank.
doc_level_aggregation='mean of token scores (paper Eq. 3)'; doc AUROC mean=0.5678, and max aggregation is also reported as a control.

The split follows the authors' recovered split_anomaly_data: n_train=int(300*0.5)=150 documents drawn from normal indices with np.random.seed(42), giving 150 test docs (120 normal + 30 anomalous). This is 50% of all documents drawn from the normal pool, not literally 50% of the normal documents (135) as the paper prose states; documented as assumption A12.
metrics.json reports token AUROC/AUPRC (0.6137/0.0380) and document AUROC/AUPRC for mean (0.5678/0.2095) and max (0.4733/0.1789) aggregation.
The clean re-run executed only TokenCore on Grammar; LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder and LUNAR were never run, so the Table 1 comparison and the ranking claim are unverified.
Word-level alignment is enforced (word_ids grouping) and the run reports 'alignment coverage 2746/2746 = 1.0'; the extractor matches the authors' align.py.
300 documents extracted, n_test_anomalous=30, test_doc_positive_rate=0.20 (i.e. 30/150), consistent with 270 normal + 30 anomalous documents.

The 30 anomalous test documents carry 47 anomalous tokens in total; document labels are taken from the released annotated benchmark, consistent with at least one anomalous token per anomalous document.
